She has been writing professionally since 2018, creating product reviews, affiliate articles, and search ads for global clients while working with Rubix Agency and Cognizant. Previously, she spent a year teaching English at the junior high level.An avid reader since childhood, Pradershika's idea of extreme sports is staying up to read “just one more chapter.” She lives in India.

Amazon's Prime Big Deal Days, the October edition of Prime Day, runs Oct. 6 and 7, and Bluetooth speaker discounts from Soundcore, Ultimate Ears, JBL, and Marshall are live. Prices range from $19.99 for the Select 4 Go to $249 for the Marshall Stanmore III, with plenty of options in between, whether you want something small enough to throw in a backpack or a larger speaker with enough volume for a backyard gathering. For more discounts and the latest offers, check out our extensive Prime Day 2026 coverage.

The Soundcore Select 4 Go is $19.99, down from $34.99, and its IP67 rating, floating design, and carrying strap make it easy to take to the beach or clip to a backpack—while the Soundcore 2 is $28.48, down from $44.99, and is better suited to a desk or kitchen, with 12W of output and up to 24 hours of playback.

For outdoor use, the Soundcore Boom Go 3i is $55.99, down from $79.99, and pairs an IP68 rating with 24 hours of playback and a battery that can charge a phone. The Soundcore Boom 2 is $84.99, down from $129.99, and steps up to a built-in subwoofer, up to 80W of output, and a floating body for a backyard or pool, which this in-depth review by PCMag breaks down further.

The Soundcore Motion X600 is $139.99, down from $199.99, and uses five drivers, including one that fires upward, to create spatial audio for listening at home. This PCMag review looks at it more closely. The Soundcore Boom 2 Plus is $161.47, down from $249.99, the largest discount in this group, and its 140W output, 20-hour battery, and floating design suit larger outdoor gatherings, as PCMag's review covers in more detail.

All four Ultimate Ears speakers here are IP67-rated for dust and water, starting with the Ultimate Ears Miniroll at $47.49, down from $79.99. It's a flat, palm-sized speaker with a silicone strap for handlebars or a bag and 12 hours of battery life, though it doesn't work with the Ultimate Ears app for EQ adjustments—this PCMag review gives a closer look at how it performs for its size. The Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4 is $56.99, down from $99.99, and adds 360-degree sound, a floating body, 14 hours of playback, and an Outdoor Boost mode for open spaces.

The Ultimate Ears Boom 4 is $99.99, down from $149.99, and keeps the cylindrical shape of earlier Boom models while switching to USB-C charging, with 360-degree sound, a floating design, and 15 hours of battery life. The Ultimate Ears Everboom is $139.99, down from $178.99, and is the most outdoor-focused of the four, with 20 hours of playback, a Bluetooth range of up to 55 meters, an Outdoor Boost button, and a carabiner for clipping it to a bag or tent.

The JBL Go 5 is $39.95 (regularly $54.95) and has an IP68 rating, up to 10 hours of playback with Playtime Boost, and AirTouch, which pairs two Go 5s for stereo when you tap them together. The JBL Clip 5 is $59.95, down from $79.95, and builds in a wide carabiner for hooking onto a bag or belt, along with an IP67 rating, up to 15 hours of playback with Playtime Boost, and EQ controls in the JBL Portable app.

The JBL Grip costs $69.95, down from $99.95, and adds an IP68 rating, Auracast, and AI Sound Boost to limit distortion at high volume. PCMag's review gives a closer look at how it sounds for its size—while the JBL Flip 5, an older model from 2019 with 20W of output, an IPX7 rating, and 12 hours of battery life is currently is $89.95, down from $99.95. This PCMag review covers it in more detail.

The JBL Charge 6 is $149.95, down from $199.95, and is the largest JBL speaker here. It's rated for 24 hours of playback plus four more with Playtime Boost, and it has an IP68 rating, a removable strap, and a built-in power bank for charging a phone. It also supports lossless audio over USB-C. For a detailed breakdown of its performance, check out this PCMag review.

The Marshall Emberton III is $99.99 (down from $179.99), pairing Marshall's amp-inspired styling with two 10W drivers, an IP67 rating, and a battery rated for more than 32 hours. There's also a built-in microphone for calls and multipoint Bluetooth support. If you like Marshall's design but don't want a speaker permanently tethered to an outlet, the Emberton III is the obvious place to start. For something larger while still staying portable, the Marshall Middleton is $149.99, down $170 from $319.99. It carries the same recognizable Marshall styling in a bigger design than the Emberton III, giving you a step up if you want more substantial sound without moving to one of the brand's plug-in home speakers.

Speaking of which, the Marshall Acton III and Marshall Stanmore III are home speakers that plug into the wall. The Acton III is $189.99, down from $299.99, and is the smallest model in Marshall's home lineup. It has 60W of amplification, Bluetooth and 3.5mm inputs, and analog bass and treble knobs on top—this PCMag's review covers in it more detail. The Stanmore III is $249, down from $399.99, and steps up to 80W while adding an RCA input, which makes it a straightforward match for a turntable with a built-in preamp. PCMag's review gives a closer look at its sound and setup.

Bose’s SoundLink Plus is currently $179, down from $269, and is built for taking your music outside, with an IP67 rating that protects it from dust and water and up to 20 hours of battery life to get you through a full day away from an outlet. PCMag’s review has more on how it sounds in practice. For more power, the larger SoundLink Max is $279 (down from $399), with the same battery life and IP67 protection, and a USB-C port that can charge another device. It’s the better fit if you want to fill a larger space with sound rather than keep things compact. This PCMag review looks into its performance in more detail. Both models are also at their lowest prices to date, according to price trackers, making either size a better buy than usual.

The compact Sony SRS-XB100 is $43, down from $64.99, making it the least expensive Sony speaker here. It's small enough to carry easily, with an IP67 rating for dust and water resistance and up to 16 hours of battery life. PCMag's review goes into more detail on its sound and performance. The Sony ULT Field 1 is $68, down from $139.99, and gives you a larger portable option without a major jump in price. It has an IP67 rating, a shock-resistant design, and up to 12 hours of battery life, while Sony's ULT button boosts the low end when you want more bass. PCMag's review takes a closer look at how it performs.

Moving up in size, the Sony ULT Field 3 is $148, down from $209.99. It extends battery life to up to 24 hours and keeps the IP67 protection and ULT bass boost, while its detachable shoulder strap makes the larger speaker easier to carry. You can read more about its sound and features in PCMag's review. The Sony ULT Field 7 is the biggest option of the group at $448, down from $499. It's built more for parties and larger spaces than tossing into a bag, with up to 30 hours of battery life, an IP67 rating, and lighting around the speaker drivers. It also has inputs for a microphone and guitar if you want to use it for karaoke or live music. PCMag's review has a closer look at its performance.

October Prime Day is Oct. 6 and runs through Oct. 7. It happens every year during October.

October Prime Day ends on Oct. 7, 2026. It’s a two-day online sale.

October Prime Day is the fall version of Prime Day, which is the biggest sale Amazon hosts during the spring, summer, and fall. You can find deals on many categories during the sale, including tech, tools, appliances, apparel, and more.

Neil Jordan’s forgotten 2012 film 'Byzantium' is the ultimate antidote to 'Twilight'

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If your idea of a vampire movie was ruined by sparkly teen romances, “Byzantium” is the antidote. It's the complete opposite of movies like "Twilight," as fun as they are. It's a moody, grown-up, gothic tale that almost nobody talks about. This 2012 film is streaming free on Tubi right now, and it comes from a director who knows the genre as well as anyone.

Directed by Neil Jordan, the Oscar winner behind “The Crying Game” and, more to the point, “Interview with the Vampire," “Byzantium” is an adaptation of Moira Buffini’s stage play starring Saoirse Ronan and Gemma Arterton as its two leads,

It's a slow, stylish, character-driven take on immortality rather than a jump-scare machine. Even better for Halloween hounds, it's a mix of delectable bloodthirst with centuries of secrets to draw from. If you want a vampire story with some true sadness to it, this is a hidden gem absolutely worth seeking out since it's available for the low, low price of free right now.

Clara (Gemma Arterton) and Eleanor (Saoirse Ronan) are a mother and daughter who arrive, broke and on the run, in a seaside town. They take refuge in a guesthouse called Byzantium, which Clara turns into a brothel to keep them afloat. What the locals don’t realize is that the two women are vampires, and that they’ve been the same age for 200 years.

Eleanor, forever a teenager, is lonely and exhausted by a lifetime of secrecy, and she longs to tell someone the truth about what she is. When she befriends Frank (Caleb Landry Jones), a sweet young man who she finds is deathly ill, she finally starts to share her story.

But opening up is dangerous, because a brotherhood of ancient male vampires has been hunting Clara and Eleanor for years, furious that the two women ever joined their ranks at all. As their past closes in, the film unravels the centuries-old history that made them what they are and why they're children of the night.

More than a horror movie, “Byzantium” is a story about women surviving in a world that keeps trying to control them. If that isn't a fable that's relevant to today's age, I don't know what is. But it's also about the loneliness of carrying a secret no one can ever know. I

Sign up to the weekly Tom's Streaming Guide to stay in the loop with the latest releases and top recommendations across your favorite streaming services. We’ve got you covered with a complete guide on what’s worth watching.

Immortality here isn’t glamorous, and instead it's a heartbreaking burden that Jordan treats with sorrow. That sets it apart from some of the more lackadaisical stories about vampirism and gives you a reason to become more emotionally invested.

Saoirse Ronan, years before her string of Oscar nominations, is fantastic as an old soul trapped in a girl’s body, and Gemma Arterton is ferocious as her mother.

At just under two hours, “Byzantium” is a beautiful, bloody, deeply melancholy vampire film that deserves a far bigger cult than it has.

If you've been looking for the perfect flick to kick off Halloween proper without relying on the same movies over and over again, this is your sign to hop onto Tubi right now.

#594. These Are the Best Last-Minute Deals on Smart Home Tech Before October Prime Day Ends Tonight

Pradershika Sharma is a tech deals writer for Lifehacker. She has a Master’s degree in English Literature, a B.Ed., and a TESOL certification. She has been writing professionally since 2018, creating product reviews, affiliate articles, and search ads for global clients while working with Rubix Agency and Cognizant. Previously, she spent a year teaching English at the junior high level.An avid reader since childhood, Pradershika's idea of extreme sports is staying up to read “just one more chapter.” She lives in India.

Amazon's October Prime Day 2026 sale has officially begun, and discounts on smart home devices are live, across just about every corner of the category, from $13 smart plugs and sub-$30 security cameras to robot vacuums with hundreds of dollars knocked off their usual prices. Whether you're looking to add a 2K/4K camera to the backyard, swap your deadbolt for a smart lock, automate a few appliances, or finally hand floor-cleaning duties over to a robot, these are the October Prime Day smart home deals worth knowing about.

A lot of these are sitting at their lowest prices on record (according to price trackers), and the range is wide enough that you could outfit a whole house for the cost of one premium robot vacuum. For more on the October Prime Day sale, you can browse more deals and sale announcements on our Prime Day Deals page.

Blink’s Wired Floodlight Camera is $29.99, down from $99.99—a 70% discount on a camera that pairs motion-triggered floodlights with 1080p video, though it needs existing wiring, according to this PCMag review.

Ring Spotlight Cam Plus is $79.99 (regularly $149.99). Also at a record low, this is the battery model, so placement is flexible, with its built-in spotlight giving you color footage at night.

For wireless options, the Eufy Security SoloCam S340 is $119.99, down from $199.99—it’s more expensive upfront, but Eufy stores footage locally, so there's no subscription bill afterward, and the solar panel means you may never charge it by hand. PCMag gave it an “excellent” rating, with its review offering a closer look at how those features perform in practice.

If you need multiple cameras, a two-pack of the Arlo Essential Wired Outdoor Camera is $59 (originally $69), its lowest price yet, which works out to just under $30 per camera. Each records in 2K and has motorized 360-degree pan and 180-degree tilt for wider coverage, though you'll need an outlet near each mounting spot, notes this PCMag review.

For even more coverage, the Tapo MagCam C460 three-pack is $199.99, down from $399.99, cutting the usual price in half. That works out to about $67 per 4K camera.

Blink Mini 2K+ is $15.99 (was $39.99). The cheapest thing on this list by a distance, and at its lowest price ever. Fine for keeping an eye on a pet or a back door, though cloud storage requires a Blink subscription.

The Ring Indoor Cam is $24.99, down from $49.99. It comes with a manual privacy shutter for when you don't want a camera watching your living space; this PCMag review goes into more detail. For only $5 more, the newer Ring Indoor Cam Plus is $29.99 (was $59.98) and bumps the resolution from 1080p to 2K. PCMag gave this model an “excellent” rating in its review. Both cameras are at their lowest prices yet.

The Eufy Security Indoor Camera E30 steps up to a 4K sensor with 360-degree pan-and-tilt and automatic tracking that follows movement around a room. It is currently $52.24, down from $69.99.

Blink Battery Doorbell 2K+ with Chime is $44.99 (was $109.98). A record low on a 2K doorbell bundled with the chime you'd otherwise buy separately, and the wire-free installation makes it renter-friendly. For more on its performance, check out this PCMag review.

At an even lower $37.99, the Chamberlain myQ Video Doorbell is down from $99.99. You can read more about it in PCMag's review.

Moving up slightly in price, the Arlo Video Doorbell 2K (2nd Gen) with Chime is $47.99 (was $69.99). Its square aspect ratio gives you a head-to-toe view of visitors while also showing packages left on the doorstep, an advantage PCMag highlights in its “excellent” review.

If you're already using other Ecobee devices, the Ecobee Smart Video Doorbell is $119.99 (was $159.99) and slots neatly into the same ecosystem. It also integrates with Apple Home, something you won't find on every doorbell in this price range. PCMag's review has more on how it works.

The Eufy Security Video Doorbell E340 Kit with Chime is $139.99 (was $219.99) and uses dual cameras: a front-facing one for visitors and a downward-facing one for packages left at your door. It also supports local storage, so you can use it without a subscription. PCMag gave it an “excellent” review.

At the top end of this group, the Ring Wired Doorbell Pro (3rd Gen) with Chime is $169.99 (was $284.98). It uses radar-based motion detection for more precise alerts, helping filter out things like passing cars. PCMag gave it an “excellent” review.

Eufy has four locks discounted, and they climb steadily in both price and ambition—the Smart Lock C220 at $94.97, down from $169.99, is the entry point and reads a fingerprint in well under a second. The Smart Lock Front Door Lever Set at $129.98, down from $189.99, replaces the handle as well as the deadbolt and is weather-rated for exposed doors, while the FamiLock E34 at $195.99, down from $279.99, swaps fingerprints for palm vein recognition, handy for when your hands are wet or cold. And at the top sits the Video Smart Lock E330 at $189.98, down from $299.99, combining a video doorbell into the deadbolt itself with local storage support.

The Philips Wi-Fi Smart Door Lock is $104.47 (was $142.49), its lowest price yet, and has a touchscreen keypad that lets you hand out temporary access codes to a cleaner, dog walker, or guest. For essentially the same price, the Philips Wi-Fi Keypad Door Lock with Handle at $104.48 (was $179.99) includes both the deadbolt and matching handle, making it the better fit if you want to replace the entire lock assembly in one go.

Tapo Smart Wi-Fi Door Lock is $108.53 (was $149.99), with fingerprint, keypad, and app entry, plus a rechargeable battery that needs a USB-C top-up once or twice a year instead of fresh AAs.

If you'd prefer to combine several front-door devices into one, the myQ Secure View 3-in-1 Smart Lock with 2K HDR Video Doorbell Camera is $142.50, down from $199.99.

iRobot has five Roombas discounted, all at record lows—the Roomba 415X is $398.99, down from $799.99, with self-emptying, self-cleaning, and obstacle avoidance that steers reliably around cables and shoes. The Roomba 505 and Roomba 505X are both $469.99, down from $999.99, sitting a tier above on navigation and mopping. The Roomba Plus 415 is $499.99, down from $599.99, while the Roomba 705X rounds out the group at $699.99, down from $1,399.99, adding an extending mop arm that reaches into corners other models skim past.

Roborock's five span the widest range of anything here—the Robot Vacuum Mop with LiDAR at $199.99, down from $299.99, packs 10,000Pa of suction and LiDAR mapping into a machine you still empty yourself, while the Qrevo S Pro at $384.99, down from $699.99, adds mop lifting for carpets and a dock that washes and dries. It is also the most well-rounded midrange pick here. Moving up, the Qrevo Edge 2 at $784.99, down from $1,299.99, and the Qrevo Edge 3 Pro at $984.99, down from $1,499.99, both use extending side brushes and mops for proper corner coverage, with the Edge 3 Pro adding stronger suction for houses mixing carpet and hard floors.

Shark's four are the value end of the category—the AI Ultra Robot Vacuum at $249.99, down from $599, gets you a self-emptying base for a fraction of what most cost, and the Matrix Plus at $229.99, down from $449.99, adds mopping and a cleaning pattern that goes over the same patch repeatedly. The Stratos and PowerDetect are both $399.99, down from $549.99, with the former offering an odor-neutralizing base that counts in a home with pets and the latter ramping suction automatically when it detects carpet or heavier debris.

Eufy's three cover the budget-to-premium span—the Omni C20 at $319.98, down from $549.99, is the cheapest route here to a dock that washes mop pads as well as emptying the bin, while the E25 at $569.98, down from $999.99, is a $400 cut on a machine whose dock runs noticeably quieter than most when emptying. At the top of Eufy's lineup here, the Omni S2 is $1,279.99 (was $1,599.99). It's still a significant investment despite the $200 discount, but you're getting Eufy's more advanced cleaning and automation features in one machine.

Ecovacs rounds out the category with two steep cuts—the Deebot T90 Pro Omni is $499, down from $799.99, taking $300 off a machine built with long hair and pet fur in mind, thanks to a brush design that resists tangling. For something more premium, the Deebot X12 Omnicyclone is $799, down from $1,499.99, a $700 discount on a model whose bagless dock means no replacement bags to keep buying.

October Prime Day discounts have brought Amazon's entire Echo smart-speaker lineup down in price, starting with the Echo Dot at $39.99, down from $79.99, still the easiest way to add voice control to a spare room, and the Echo Spot at $54.99, down from $109.99, which adds a small display that makes it a better bedside clock. The Echo Dot Max at $79.99, down from $119.99, has enough low end to work as a real kitchen music speaker, and the Echo Studio at $179.99, down from $219.99 and its lowest price yet, is the only Echo genuinely built for listening instead of just asking about the weather. All of these support the AI assistant Alexa+.

The Echo Show displays are discounted across the range too, and they scale by where you plan to put them—the Echo Show 5 at $59.99, down from $99.99, is nightstand-sized, while the Echo Show 8 at $124.99, down from $199.99, reaches the point where recipes and video calls become readable from across a counter. The Echo Show 11 at $149.99, down from $249.99, splits the difference, and the wall-mounted Echo Show 15 at $249.99, down from $349.99, is built to serve as a family calendar and note board. The Echo Show 21 at $349.99, down from $499.99, is large enough to double as a small kitchen TV. All of these support the AI assistant Alexa+.

Amazon’s Smart Thermostat is $56.99 (was $79.99), and is the cheapest way to get scheduling and remote control, though it has no built-in display worth speaking of and leans on the app.

Ecobee Smart Thermostat Enhanced is $164.99 (was $199.99), with support for remote room sensors, so the temperature reflects where people actually are instead of the hallway.

Amazon Smart Plug is $12.98 (was $24.99). A record low, and the simplest way to put a lamp or coffee maker on a schedule.

Kasa’s Smart Plug Power Strip KP303 is $24.98 (was $29.98), and it gives you three independently controlled outlets plus surge protection, useful behind a TV stand.

Eightree 5GHz Smart Plug (4-Pack) is $33.99 (was $39.99). Four plugs for the price of one Hue, with energy monitoring and 5GHz support that many cheap plugs lack.

Tapo’s Smart Wi-Fi Power Strip is $39.99 (was $49.99), and with Matter support, it works across Alexa, Google Home, and Apple Home instead of locking you into any one ecosystem.

October Prime Day (actually called "Prime Big Deal Days") begins Oct. 6 and runs through Oct. 7. This is one of three major Amazon sales throughout the year, and it happens every year during October.

Prime Day sales, include Prime Big Deal Days, let Prime Members shop online for thousands of products with big discounts. It only lasts two days, so make sure you check out everything we know about the sale.

Since Prime Big Deal Days happens in the fall, you're likely to see more deals on gaming and indoor gym equipment. Amazon has already announced some of the 35 categories that will be on sale, including beauty, tech, kitchen, fashion, and home. Some brands Amazon has already mentioned are: Shark, Princess Polly, Soundcore by Anker, UGG, Nest New York, Sony, Tarte, Adidas, and Barefoot Dreams.

#595. These Are the Best Last-Minute October Prime Day Deals on Home Improvement Tools

Becca Lewis is home maintenance writer who aims to foster confidence in and inspire DIY enthusiasts at all skill levels.

Becca attended Southern Connecticut State University, where she studied technical theater and design. She has a background in carpentry and fabrication and has worked in specialty shops, using a wide variety of tools and materials, for more than 20 years.

Becca has also written for Angi, where she specializes in creating guides for DIY, home maintenance, and renovations, and she indulges her love of sci-fi and fantasy by writing about entertainment and science for Giant Freakin Robot. She serves on the board of the Good Junk Sanctuary in Portland, Oregon, focusing on community engagement in the DIY and reuse space.

If you need to tackle some DIY projects this fall, you might be looking to beef up your DIY tool kit. But if you’ve looked for tools recently, you may have noticed that high-quality tools that will last can be expensive. Here are some deals on some of my favorite tools during Amazon’s Big Deal Days sale.

If you’re just starting out on your DIY adventure, beginning with a tool set will give you a solid foundation. Here are some deals on quality tools that will be with you for years to come.

The DeWalt 20-volt oscillating multitool set is on sale for $157, 47% off its regular price. The set comes with the multitool, a 2-amp-hour battery, a charger, three starter blades, a sanding attachment, and some sandpaper. This tool can be used to cut metal, wood, plaster, drywall, PVC, and tile, and you can also use it for sanding and polishing. It’s a good deal for expanding your existing DeWalt set or if you’re just starting out with DIY projects.

The DeWalt 192-piece mechanic’s tool set is on sale for $169.94, 41% off its usual price. This set comes with ½-inch, ⅜-inch, and ¼-inch ratchets, sockets in SAE and metric sizes, a set of spark plug sockets, driver bits, a set of hex wrenches, and adapters. This is a full tool set that will allow you to work on cars, as well as do maintenance on small home appliances like changing filters and replacing hoses.

The Craftsman 10-piece mechanics tool set is on sale for $14.99, 51% off its typical price. The set comes with a ⅜-inch ratchet and nine metric sockets. This compact set is good for most beginner DIY projects and can be used for light vehicle maintenance; it's also perfect for an emergency roadside kit.

Saws are essential for many DIY projects, like repairing fencing or building shelves, and they’re also excellent for yard work and demolition. Having the right tools for making precision cuts will make your projects go more smoothly. Here are some deals on saws for all your DIY needs.

The DeWalt 7 ¼-inch cordless compound miter saw is on sale for $296.65, 20% off its regular price. This is a tool-only deal, so you’ll need a DeWalt 20-volt battery and charger to use it. This saw is compact and portable so it’s useful for situations where you don’t have a permanent home shop set up. You can use it to cut molding and trim for door frames, stairs, and finishing decks.

The Husqvarna 14-inch 225i battery-powered chainsaw is on sale for $264.99, 30% off its regular price. The saw comes with a chain, a battery, and a charger. It can make up to 190 cuts on a single charge, and you can use it to cut up downed tree limbs and clear thick branches.

The DeWalt 20-volt jigsaw is on sale for $139.90, 41% off its usual price. This is a tool-only deal, so you’ll need a DeWalt 20-volt battery and charger to use it. A jigsaw can be used to cut curves and irregular shapes and is useful for making specialty cuts in fencing or for making decorative cuts on decor or furniture.

Bits and accessories for your power tools don’t seem like they’ll be a big expense until you’ve made your third trip to the hardware store for a size you don’t have on hand. Here are some of the best deals on bits and accessories.

The DeWalt 35-piece impact bit set is on sale for $29.98, 66% off its regular price. The set comes with a bit holder, a socket adapter, several types of driver tips, and a set of sockets. It’s a good set for driving fasteners, but you’ll need drill bits if you want to drill holes.

The Bosch 41-piece drilling and driving combo set is on sale for $21.47, 57% off its usual price. This set comes with drill bits up to ¾”, several types of driver tips, an adapter, and a case. This bit set is a good starter set because it has both driver tips and drill bits, so you could use it with a drill for hanging pictures or curtains, or for assembling flat-packed furniture.

The Milwaukee socket adapter set is on sale for $8.21, 47% off its regular price. This set comes with socket adapters for ¼-inch, ½-inch, and ⅜-inch sockets. This is a tool that you won’t know you need until you don’t have it. I use mine all the time to switch between driving screws and driving nuts for installing wheels and assembling metal parts.

'Bed bugs are purely opportunistic' — pest control expert Lyuben Kiryakov shares 6 key steps to protect your mattress and bedding, and why DIY chemical sprays actually cause bugs to spread faster

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Experts have warned that more bed bugs than ever before are circulating through travel. The current global outbreak reached a crescendo this week, grounding a Qantas plane flying from Rome to Perth, forcing a US school closure and halting a UK rail service when bed bugs were spotted in classrooms and on the train. “We are at peak bed bug,” Martim Gois, the co-founder of Valpas, a company which produces technology to trap and track bed bugs in hotel rooms, told The Times this week. “Bedbugs correlate with traveller volume. The more arrivals and departures there are, the higher the surge of bedbugs,” said Gois. With bed bug outbreaks left, right and center, you might be wondering what you can do to protect your home from the critters and derail them from finding their way to your mattress. We spoke to a bed bug prevention and control specialist to find out, plus identify which home and behavior type is most at risk of succumbing to an infestation.

Anyone can fall foul of a bed bug outbreak. However, there are certain habits and circumstances that can increase our risk. They are:

“Bed bugs are strictly indoor pests, meaning they are entirely unaffected by outdoor weather conditions,” Lyuben Kiryakov, Director of pest control agency Bed Bug Specialist, tells Tom's Guide. “However, human behaviour changes significantly with the seasons. During the summer months, people travel far more frequently. Staying in infested hotels, hostels, or short term rentals is one of the primary ways people pick up an infestation. “Bed bugs are purely opportunistic," Kiryakov continues. "Given the first chance, they will crawl directly into luggage, clothing, and personal belongings to be carried home."

According to Kiryakov, there is one particular home type that is most at risk from the current outbreak: “Blocks of flats [apartments] are significantly more vulnerable to bed bugs than single family houses, primarily due to the widespread use of ineffective DIY treatments.”

“Insecticide sprays, powders, and smoke bombs often agitate bed bugs rather than killing them, causing the infestation to scatter through wall voids, electrical sockets, and structural gaps into adjacent flats."Residents also tend to leave infested furniture directly outside their building or in communal areas, from where they can easily hitch a ride back inside on other residents and spread the infestation further," says Kiryakov.

Bed bugs are opportunistic critters that have one goal in mind: to inhabit your mattress. Here, they can hide out of sight while staying close to their food source —you.

At night they'll crawl out and bite you while you're sleeping. Here's how to protect your mattress and bedding from bed bugs:

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

"Bed bugs reproduce quickly, and an isolated issue can turn into a full scale home infestation," says Kiryakov. So if you think that you're at risk of bed bugs, don't wait to get bitten before taking action. Inspect your mattress now for signs of bed bugs, paying close attention to any creases or seams, where bed bugs like to hide. Live insects are reddish brown in color, oval shaped, and measure approximately 5-7mm. Additionally, look out for dark specs (bed bug poop), as well as live eggs. These look like grains of rice.

Even if you haven't found signs of bed bugs, giving your mattress a thorough clean with a vacuum is highly recommended. "Use a high powered hoover to meticulously capture bed bugs and eggs along mattress seams, bed frames, and skirting boards, immediately sealing and throwing away the hoover bag or emptying the canister," says Kiryakov, who notes that bed bugs are becoming resistant to insecticides.

If you don't opt for full coverage of your mattress during a bed bug outbreak, even the best mattress protectors can leave you vulnerable to infestation. For proper protection, we recommend buying a fully zippered mattress encasement. If there are bed bugs in your mattress, covering them with a full encasement means they will be starved of their food source (your blood) and die off.

A mattress encasement also provides a barrier to bed bugs taking up residence in your mattress in the first place. So if there's an outbreak in your area, this is your first step to keep your bed safe.

The urge to come in after a busy day and collapse straight onto your bed might be strong — but don't. Wearing your outdoor clothes – the ones that have been pressed up against public spaces, such as buses and trains and communal seating – could give bed bugs a one way ticket to their forever home (your mattress). Instead, change out of your outdoor clothes in a separate room. If you think there's a high chance you came into contact with bed bugs, wash your clothes at a minimum temperature of 60°C (140°F) to kill bed bugs and their eggs.

"Prevention is better than cure," says Kiryakov. "When traveling, thoroughly inspect hotel rooms, hostels, or short term rentals before unpacking, specifically checking the mattress, bed frame, headboard, and any soft seating areas."When you get home, refrain from placing your suitcase directly on your bed to unpack. Instead, put it in your bathtub, where bed bugs can't escape — the sides are too slippery for them. Remove your clothes from there and place them on a hot wash.

Heat and active removal are your best shot at removing bed bugs and their eggs before an active outbreak takes hold in your mattress and bedding.

If you feel at risk of having brought bed bugs home with you, give your bed sheets a hot wash today.To kill bed bug and their eggs, you need to launder your sheets at 60°C (140°F). Then throw them in the tumble dryer for good measure as "direct dry heat kills bed bugs and their eggs on contact," says Kiryakov.

Pay attention to the care label, as some delicate fabrics won't stand up to very hot washing and machine drying.

❌ Don't use DIY foggers, sprays or powders: "Instead of eliminating the infestation, DIY insecticides agitate the bed bugs and cause them to scatter deeper into wall voids, electrical sockets, and adjacent rooms," says Kiryakov.❌ Don't immediately ditch your mattress: The temptation to toss every soft furnishing you own will be strong, but moving your furniture around risks spreading the infestation. Instead, a professional can likely treat and save your mattress. However if your bed is over eight years old or shows signs of sagging and deep staining, then a new mattress could be in order. The changing seasons can really affect your mood, especially as we move from those long days and warm evenings of summer into the cozy fall season.

That's why your routine may need a switch-up, too. Maybe your body is craving a slower approach, or you just want to try something new. To help you, YogaRenew instructor Melie Purdon shares four yoga poses to help you feel grounded, energized and present as the weather cools.

Wherever you choose to practice, these poses will help you feel calm, centered and ready to welcome the crisp fall air. This short routine is beginner-friendly and low-impact, which means you can build foundational strength while putting less stress and strain on your joints.

One of the best yoga mats is also recommended, and that's all.

Yoga improves mobility and flexibility and strengthens your body using your body weight and some props like blocks and straps. It helps shift your body into the parasympathetic nervous system, which can reduce stress and anxiety and boost relaxation.

As the seasons change, particularly from summer to fall, grounding practices can help you manage the transition more seamlessly, especially if you find yourself sensitive to this.

Yoga is unlikely to overload the muscles in a way that builds maximal strength and muscle (you'd need to consider lifting weights several times per week), but it improves functional strength without weights and helps maintain healthy muscles, bones, joints and ligaments.

If you experience pain at any time, stop and rest. If you're working with an injury or health condition, I recommend seeking advice from your physician or a yoga instructor before starting these exercises.

Benefits: "Twists are inherently invigorating, combining strong legs, spinal extension, and torso rotation to help you feel awake and energized," says Purdon. "It's the perfect pairing with crisp fall air, especially when practicing outdoors and taking in the changing scenery."

Benefits: "This forward fold combines strong, active legs with a quiet head, offering a chance to slow down while keeping your body engaged," Purdon says. "Between work, apple picking, school schedules, and Halloween costume crafting, sometimes the best way to reset is to give your body something specific to focus on."

Benefits: "Often called the 'King of Asanas,' headstand demands full concentration and can leave experienced practitioners feeling focused and invigorated. The combination of balance, stability, and a completely different perspective makes it a powerful way to reconnect with the present moment," says Purdon.

"Practice this advanced pose with guidance from a qualified yoga teacher rather than relying on written instructions alone."

This is the only exercise that isn't beginner-friendly, but you can still play around with it while keeping your feet firmly on the ground to get benefits and stay playful.

Benefits: "Supported bridge opens the front of the body and offers a moment of relief from the tension that builds up after hours of sitting, working, and running around," Purdon explains. "With the block supporting your sacrum, you can ease into stillness without having to hold yourself up.

"If you're practicing outdoors, take a few minutes to enjoy the changing leaves and let the demands of the day fade into the background."

Ah, stretching versus mobility. It's a debate that never ends. As a coach who focuses most of my time on teaching mobility classes to people of all ages, I am a little biased, but I can tell you that while stretching can be beneficial (certain types, and when done properly, for muscle flexibility), mobility training will move the needle most for anti-aging and joint health.

I recently put together this 20-minute mobility routine you can do at home using the best yoga mat and your bodyweight. You don't need equipment, but bands and light weights are optional; it depends on how much experience you already have with the movements.

Check out the moves below and what you can expect from your body over time.

As you age, strong bones, muscles, and ligaments help you stay active, whether that's gardening, playing with your kids (and grandkids), hitting the gym, or running the track.

I encourage at least two strength sessions per week, along with daily mobility work, even if that means a bodyweight or calisthenics routine rather than lifting heavy weights.

If you experience pain at any time, stop and rest. If you're working with an injury or health condition, I recommend seeking advice before starting these exercises.
